title: Hybrid sterility resembles sterility caused by unnatural conditions

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Hybrid sterility resembles sterility caused by unnatural conditions

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The sterility of hybrids closely resembles the sterility induced in pure species by unnatural conditions of life: in both cases the reproductive system is disturbed independently of general health, by disturbed conditions in one case and by two organisations compounded into one in the other.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Thus we see that when organic beings are placed under new and unnatural conditions, and when hybrids are produced by the unnatural crossing of two species, the reproductive system, independently of the general state of health, is affected by sterility in a very similar manner.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter VIII, “Hybridism”; section “Causes of the sterility of first crosses and of hybrids”. Scope: hybrids and pure species under captivity or cultivation

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch08-10: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.61

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Parallel reproductive phenotypes and molecular pathways can be compared with existing datasets. Confounding and Darwin's broad environmental category make the causal analogy only partly resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare reproductive output, general-health measures, gonadal pathology, and expression profiles between hybrids and pure species exposed to captivity or environmental stress. Shared reproductive-specific disruption supports the proposed resemblance.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Unnatural conditions' covers heterogeneous treatments.

Phenotypic resemblance does not establish a shared causal mechanism.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data existence: 0.74
data adequacy: 0.5
discriminating power: 0.5
analysis feasibility: 0.58

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The parallel is testable in principle with matched measures of gonad function and general health, and fragments of both literatures exist. No public dataset lines up captive sterility with hybrid sterility, so data existence stays low and a harmonized analysis would be slow. Even a matched pattern would be confounded by the many unrelated ways captivity reduces breeding.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare, across taxa, whether captivity and hybridization both impair gametogenesis while leaving general health intact. A shared pattern restricted to the reproductive system would support the resemblance; sterility in captivity that tracks nutrition, behavior, or whole-body illness, unlike hybrid incompatibilities, would weaken it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Resemblance of outcomes does not show resemblance of causes.

Zoo and studbook records that would measure captive sterility are not openly downloadable.

Hybrid and captivity studies rarely use the same taxa and the same health measures.

data existence: 0.38
